description: Round-2's fix for prior FIND-002 relabeled ONLY PROP-5 and PROP-6 in specs/verification-architecture.md from a bare 'T2' (= the tier legend's 'integration/property (no-mock)', verification-architecture.md:3) to an honest 'T1 (wiring, injected seam)' — but the identical defect (a required PROP claiming the no-mock T2 tier while its ONLY test drives the SAME ARTICLE_TEST_FORCE_V0/ARTICLE_TEST_FORCE_V05 injected-seam mechanism that short-circuits gates/v0.sh's and gates/v05.sh's real logic before it ever runs, per gates/v0.sh:18-26 and gates/v05.sh:46-56) still stands, unfixed, in TWO OTHER required (required=✅) proof obligations: PROP-13 and PROP-15. (1) PROP-13 (verification-architecture.md:35: 'Mode B: when V0∧V0.5 PASS, the skill publishes DIRECTLY... | T2 | ✅') is exercised only by tests/test-prop2-no-human-modeB.sh's Mode-B dynamic check (lines 15-19: `AUTONOMY=on ... ARTICLE_TEST_V0_RESULTS="PASS" ARTICLE_TEST_V05_RESULTS="PASS"`), which run.sh:159-161 translates directly into `ARTICLE_TEST_FORCE_V0=PASS`/`ARTICLE_TEST_FORCE_V05=PASS` env vars for gates/v0.sh and gates/v05.sh — the exact same bypass FIND-002 identified for PROP-5/6, never exercising the real gate mechanics. (2) PROP-15 (verification-architecture.md:37: 'after 3 consecutive V0/V0.5 FAILs the wake ABORTS... (ceiling test: stub 3 fails → assert abort...) | T2 | ✅') is exercised only by tests/test-prop15-3round-abort.sh (lines 10-16: `ARTICLE_TEST_V0_RESULTS="PASS,PASS,PASS" ARTICLE_TEST_V05_RESULTS="FAIL,FAIL,FAIL"`), the same injected-seam mechanism — and PROP-15's OWN row text even says 'stub 3 fails', directly contradicting its own 'T2'/no-mock tier label in the same row. This is not a one-off miss: the round-2 fix addressed the two PROPs named literally in FIND-002's text but did not generalize the fix to every required PROP that shares the identical injected-seam test mechanism, so the verification-tier claims a fresh reader (or Phase 6 convergence check) relies on for PROP-13/PROP-15 remain false in exactly the way FIND-002 was raised to correct.
